column1: What does machine learning say about the drivers of inflation?

The thesis titled What does machine learning say about the drivers of inflation? by Emanuel Kohlscheen  published as BIS Working Paper No. 980  explores the factors influencing Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation using a machine learning approach. The study focuses on 20 advanced economies over the period from 2000 to 2021  employing a computationally intensive method involving 1 000 regression trees based on six key macroeconomic variables. This data-driven  non-parametric method  specifically the random forest technique  is used to predict inflation outcomes and is noted for its strong predictive performance  surpassing traditional econometric models in terms of out-of-sample root mean square errors (RMSE).

The paper highlights the significant role of inflation expectations in determining CPI outcomes  although their influence has diminished over the past decade. The study also finds that exchange rate variations contribute minimally to inflation predictions. The research builds on existing literature that applies machine learning to economic prediction  emphasizing the advantages of non-parametric methods in capturing non-linear relationships in data. The random forest model's success in predicting inflation is attributed to its ability to handle non-linearities effectively  which are crucial in understanding the dynamics of inflation.

The study contributes to the broader literature by reaffirming the importance of expectations in the inflation process and highlighting the role of non-linearities in economic modeling. It also underscores the significance of global factors  such as oil prices and global Producer Price Index (PPI) inflation  in influencing CPI inflation  particularly after 2010. The findings support the relevance of current inflation targeting frameworks and suggest that policies play a crucial role in managing inflation trends.

The paper is structured as follows: Section 1 introduces the research questions and the significance of understanding inflation drivers. Section 2 details the methodology and dataset used for predicting inflation. Section 3 presents the baseline results  demonstrating the superior performance of the random forest model. Section 4 explores the changing dynamics of inflation drivers over time. The study concludes by emphasizing the potential of machine learning techniques in enhancing our understanding of inflation and informing economic policy.
